correctness.rationale: For all integers \(a,b\ge2\), the known transfer-current determinantal theorem gives covariance entries from \(K=B^{\mathsf T}L^+B\). Decomposing the bipartite vertex Laplacian into its left/right zero-sum and partition-contrast eigenspaces gives \(K_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}=\mathbf1_{\{i=k\}}/b+\mathbf1_{\{j=\ell\}}/a-1/(ab)\). Directly squaring its off-diagonal entries yields four covariance orbits. Exact orthogonal row/column/interaction projectors reproduce the entire operator, giving its rank, eigenvalues, all-weight variance, linear-degree projection residual, and sharp bounds. The proof checks the boundary \(a=b=2\) and dimension/multiplicity accounting. A standalone rational verifier exhausts six parameter cases (4657 trees; 597 covariance entries and 2388 projector checks), not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the fully evaluated four-eigenspace covariance spectrum for edge membership in uniform bipartite spanning trees, and the resulting sharp variance and degree-linear-projection geometry for every cost matrix. Pairwise transfer-current covariance identities and vertex-degree generating functions are attributed and not asserted as new. Exact statement/implication comparisons of accessed principal sources found no asserted identical or dominating evaluated all-weight spectrum. Possible implicit historical derivations remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The sample-dependent cost of a uniform spanning tree is a fundamental linear network statistic. The theorem evaluates its variance for every real cost array, shows exactly which uncertainties are visible to vertex degree counts and what remains orthogonal, and provides sharp optimal/worst-case variance directions. The spectral condition number separates balanced from highly unbalanced bipartite networks, giving interpretable structural information rather than a generic pairwise probability or an arbitrary small numeric special case.
